lines.cap: **Narrator:** This is Kavya. She is twelve. It is double Science, and she has been given goggles.
**Kavya:** Every Year 8 since forever has worn these goggles. They smell like other people's faces.
**Narrator:** Her task: **neutralise** an acid. Add alkali, drop by drop, until the indicator turns green.
**Narrator:** But this documentary is not about Kavya. It's about what's happening in her beaker.
**Narrator:** Down here, there's a small family business. Neutral Ground: weddings for acids and alkalis.
**Indi:** Hi. Indi. **Universal indicator**. I'm the wedding planner.
**Indi:** I'm also the mood lighting. I change colour with **pH**. Right now I'm red, so it's very **acidic** in here.
**Indi:** People say I'm moody. I don't have moods. I have a pH.
**Indi:** Thirty beakers a lesson. Same couple in every one. Acid. Alkali. Somebody always cries.
**Indi:** And nothing starts until she picks up the dropper. We call her the Giant.
**Narrator:** Neutral Ground. Episode eight: The Wedding Crasher.
**Hal:** Hal! **Hydrochloric acid**! The groom! **pH one**!
**Indi:** Hal is an **acid**. He brought his own spotlight.
**Narrator:** An **acid** releases **hydrogen ions**, **H⁺**, in water. That's why acids taste **sour**.
**Hal:** Sour and PROUD! Lemons! Vinegar! Your STOMACH!
**Indi:** His cousins are. **Citric acid** in lemons, **ethanoic acid** in vinegar. Hal's the one in your stomach.
**Narrator:** And here comes the bride. By dropper.
**Natalie:** Natalie. **Sodium hydroxide**. I'm an **alkali**. Please wipe your feet.
**Natalie:** I release **hydroxide ions**, I feel **soapy**, and I'm in half the cleaning cupboard.
**Indi:** Natalie has wiped this beaker four times. It's full of liquid.
**Narrator:** A **base** can **neutralise** an acid. Many bases are **metal oxides** or **hydroxides**.
**Natalie:** And an **alkali** is a base that **dissolves in water**. A **soluble base**. Like me.
**Natalie:** Unlike my cousin, **copper oxide**. A base, but she won't dissolve. She just sits at the bottom. Sulking.
**Indi:** So **all alkalis are bases**, but **not all bases are alkalis**.
**Narrator:** Acids and alkalis are measured on the **pH scale**, from **zero** to **fourteen**.
**Indi:** **Below seven** is acidic. The **lower** the number, the **more acidic**. **Seven** is neutral, like pure water. **Above seven** is alkaline.
**Hal:** So if I get to pH FOURTEEN, I'm the most acidic acid EVER!
**Indi:** No.
**Indi:** **Higher** means more **alkaline**, Hal. Fourteen is Natalie's end. One is the most acidic.
**Hal:** One. Number ONE. I'll take it.
**Narrator:** Every wedding needs a colour scheme. Indi is the colour scheme.
**Indi:** An **indicator** changes **colour** with pH: acidic, neutral or alkaline, at a glance.
**Indi:** My cousin **Litmus** only does **red in acid** and **blue in alkali**. No numbers. Bless her.
**Indi:** I'm a **universal indicator**: a **mixture of dyes**. I do the whole rainbow.
**Indi:** **Red**, about pH zero to two. **Orange**, three to four. **Yellow**, five to six. All acidic.
**Indi:** **Green** at **seven**. Neutral. My favourite. Very calming.
**Indi:** Then **blue**, eight to eleven, and **purple**, twelve to fourteen. Alkaline.
**Hal:** Indi! Come here! Look! RED!
**Natalie:** Indi, darling, over here. Purple.
**Indi:** Please stop.
**Hal:** Did I mention I'm a **strong** acid? Because I'm SO **concentrated**!
**Indi:** Those are two different things, Hal.
**Narrator:** **Strength** is how fully an acid **ionises**, or splits into ions, in water. **Strong**: fully. **Weak**: only partly.
**Narrator:** **Concentration** is how much acid is in the water. Lots: **concentrated**. A little: **dilute**.
**Indi:** Today, Hal is **strong** but **dilute**. Nobody gives Year 8 the scary stuff.
**Narrator:** Concentrated acids and alkalis are often **corrosive**: they destroy skin and eyes. Dilute ones may be **irritants**.
**Indi:** So a **dilute strong** acid can be **safer** than a **concentrated weak** one.
**Kavya:** Hence the face goggles. And no, I was NOT going to taste it.
**Narrator:** Kavya picks up the dropper. The ceremony begins.
**Indi:** Dearly beloved. We are gathered here today for a **neutralisation**.
**Indi:** An **acid** and a **base** react and cancel out. The pH moves towards **seven**.
**Indi:** **Acid + base → salt + water**. A, B, S, W.
**Hal:** I, Hal, give you... my **hydrogen ions**!
**Natalie:** And I give you my **hydroxide ions**. Freshly washed.
**Narrator:** Each **H⁺** from the acid joins an **OH⁻** from the alkali, to make **water**, **H₂O**.
**Indi:** And everyone else becomes the salt. **Hydrochloric acid + sodium hydroxide → sodium chloride + water**.
**Natalie:** Sodium chloride? Like... table salt?
**Indi:** Yes. You're table salt now. Congratulations.
**Indi:** But amounts matter. Too **little** alkali, and some acid is left over. Still acidic. Keep going, Giant.
**Indi:** Just right, and I go **green**. pH seven. Beautiful. Nobody touch anything.
**Kavya:** Oh. Oops. I squeezed it a bit.
**Indi:** Too **much**, and it's **alkaline**. Mixing doesn't automatically give pH seven. That's why you need me.
**Indi:** And it's not just watering down. It's a **chemical reaction** that makes **new substances**.
**Narrator:** **Indigestion tablets** use a base to neutralise **excess stomach acid**. Farmers spread **lime**, a base, on **acidic soil**.
**Kavya:** So that's what my dad eats after chilli crab.
**Narrator:** Then the teacher hands out **magnesium** ribbon.
**Maggie:** Did somebody say ACID?! Maggie! **Magnesium**! I'm a **metal**, and I am SO ready!
**Narrator:** Magnesium **fizzes** in dilute acid. The bubbles are **hydrogen gas**.
**Henry:** Oh. Hello. Henry. **Hydrogen**. I was the H in H C L. I was the best man.
**Henry:** Then she pushed me out. Now I'm just... bubbles.
**Indi:** **Acid + metal → salt + hydrogen**. The metal takes hydrogen's place.
**Narrator:** **Hydrochloric acid + magnesium → magnesium chloride + hydrogen**.
**Maggie:** I didn't crash it! I **reacted** with it! Totally different! Is there cake?
**Narrator:** To test for **hydrogen**, hold a **lit splint** at the mouth of the tube.
**Henry:** Not the splint. Please. Not the splint.
**Henry:** POP! ...Ouch.
**Indi:** A **squeaky pop**: a little hydrogen, **burning explosively**. Every time.
**Narrator:** A salt's **first** name comes from the **metal**. Its **second** comes from the **acid**.
**Indi:** **Hydrochloric** acid makes **chlorides**. **Sulfuric** acid makes **sulfates**. **Nitric** acid makes **nitrates**.
**Indi:** So **zinc + sulfuric acid → zinc sulfate + hydrogen**. Sulfate. Not sulfide. Different wedding.
**Narrator:** Every wedding has a seating plan. For metals, it's called the **reactivity series**.
**Indi:** **Most reactive** at the top table. **Least reactive** by the door.
**Narrator:** From the top: **potassium**, **sodium**, **calcium**, **magnesium**, **aluminium**, **zinc**, **iron**. Then **hydrogen**. Then **copper**, **silver** and **gold**.
**Indi:** Remember it with: **P**lease **S**top **C**alling **M**e **A** **Z**ebra, **I**nstead **C**all **S**ome **G**old.
**Henry:** I'm not a metal. I'm the **line**. Metals **above** me react with dilute acids. Metals **below** me don't.
**Henry:** It's the most important job I've ever had.
**Narrator:** Now, four metals in the same dilute acid.
**Maggie:** Magnesium! Fizzing **vigorously**! WOOO!
**Narrator:** **Zinc** gives a **steady** fizz. **Iron**, a **slow** one. And **copper**...
**Narrator:** Nothing. Copper is **below hydrogen**. No reaction at all.
**Auntie Goldie:** Darling, I'm **gold**. Bottom of the list. I don't react with dilute acid, or water, or gossip.
**Auntie Goldie:** People dig me up as a **pure metal**. I never bothered reacting with anything. It's called class.
**Narrator:** And at the top table: **potassium**. Kept in a jar, **under oil**.
**Kavya:** Why is he in a jar?
**Indi:** **Potassium** and **sodium** react **fast** with **cold water**. He gets... excited.
**Narrator:** **Metal + water → metal hydroxide + hydrogen**. **Sodium + water → sodium hydroxide + hydrogen**.
**Natalie:** Sodium hydroxide! That's me! That's why the water left behind is **alkaline**!
**Narrator:** At the after-party, Kavya drops an **iron** nail into blue **copper sulfate** solution.
**Indi:** Iron is **more reactive** than copper, so it **pushes** copper out of its compound. That's **displacement**.
**Narrator:** **Iron + copper sulfate → iron sulfate + copper**.
**Indi:** Watch. The **blue fades**, and a **brown coating of copper** appears on the nail.
**Indi:** It never works the other way. Copper in iron sulfate? Nothing.
**Narrator:** Same idea: heating iron **ore** with **carbon**, which is more reactive, **extracts** the iron.
**Narrator:** Then a late guest: a marble chip. **Calcium carbonate**.
**Indi:** Acid + metal **carbonate** gives **three** products: **salt + water + carbon dioxide**.
**Narrator:** **Hydrochloric acid + calcium carbonate → calcium chloride + water + carbon dioxide**.
**Henry:** Bubbles?! Is that me? Please say it's not me.
**Indi:** Not you, Henry. It's **carbon dioxide**. A lit splint goes out, and **limewater** turns **milky**.
**Henry:** Oh, thank goodness.
**Maggie:** In **oxygen**, I **burn** with a **bright white flame**! **Magnesium + oxygen → magnesium oxide**!
**Indi:** Don't look straight at her. Seriously.
**Narrator:** And the third gas test: **oxygen relights** a **glowing** splint.
**Indi:** Wedding favours: salt crystals! React acid with **excess** base, **filter**, **evaporate** some water, then **cool** it slowly.

chapters.title: The wedding party saves you some marks

lines.cap: **Narrator:** Before the credits, the wedding party has some free marks.
**Maggie:** One! Acid plus metal gives **hydrogen**! Only **carbonates** give carbon dioxide!
**Henry:** Two. A **squeaky pop** means hydrogen. **Milky limewater** means carbon dioxide.
**Hal:** Three! **Concentration** is not **strength**! Dilute strong can be safer than concentrated weak!
**Natalie:** Four. **Not all bases are alkalis**. Only the soluble ones. Sorry, copper oxide.
**Indi:** Five. Litmus is **red in acid**, **blue in alkali**. And a **higher** pH is more **alkaline**.
**Hal:** Six! Neutralisation always makes **water**, as well as the **salt**!
**Auntie Goldie:** Seven. **Copper**, **silver** and **gold** don't fizz with dilute acids, darling. We're **below hydrogen**.
**Indi:** Eight. **Sulfuric** acid makes **sulfates**. Not sulfides.
**Narrator:** Neutral Ground will return.
**Kavya:** Wait. Who's the guy in the jar?
**Indi:** That's Potassium. He's not allowed near weddings. Or water.
**Potassium:** ...Is that... water?
**Henry:** Oh! Here, have some of my...
**Indi:** NO, HENRY, DON'T!
